files.reason: Full 2016 sustainability report; GRI data tables (PDF p42-46) give 2016 site-level withdrawal by source, make-up water, recycling, discharge; p31 water-use intensity by site 2015-2016; corporate production 2015-2016
2017 GRI data tables: site-level 2017 water used / discharged without use by source, recycling, discharge; corporate 2015-2017 (2015-2016 restated); corporate production 2016-2017
2018 GRI data tables (GRI 303:2018 format): site-level withdrawal by source incl. water-stressed areas, new water for processing, recycling, discharge by destination; no production table

2019 GRI data tables incl. acquired Tahoe sites (Timmins, Shahuindo, La Arena): site-level withdrawal by source incl. precipitation and water-stressed areas, new water, recycling, discharge by destination; no production table

observations: Methodology change 2017: the 2017 GRI tables introduced a company-wide water balance splitting 'water used' from 'water discharged without use' (largely mine dewatering and Morococha tailings flow-through), and restated 2015-2016 accordingly (303-1 footnote 1, 2017 file p4). The 2016 report instead split withdrawal into mine dewatering / other groundwater / surface water, so 2016 site figures are not directly comparable to the 2017 layout.

Minor restatement of 2016 new/used water: 2016 report site 'Processing Plant (make-up water)' values (PDF p44) sum to 7,153,792 m3, whereas the 2017 report gives 2016 corporate 'Water Used' total as 7,145,187 m3 (p4). 2016 production figures (25.4 Moz Ag, 183.9 koz Au, 51.9 kt Zn, 20.2 kt Pb, 14.4 kt Cu) are identical in both reports.

Format change 2018 (GRI 303:2018): tables switch to mine dewatering / groundwater / surface water withdrawal, a separate 'areas with water stress' block (only Dolores), 'new water for mineral processing' and discharge by destination (surface, groundwater, treatment plant/lagoons, third party). No explicit total-withdrawal figure is stated in 2018 or 2019; the 'Total' column of the by-source rows EXCLUDES Dolores, whose withdrawal is shown only in the water-stress block. No consumption figure is disclosed in any file.

Scope change 2019: Tahoe Resources acquisition (completed Feb 2019) adds Timmins (Canada), Shahuindo and La Arena (Peru) to the 2019 tables; energy/land tables footnote 'Including newly acquired Tahoe operations' and give a 'Silver Segment' comparison, but the water tables give no like-for-like legacy total. Corporate recycled process water rose from 16,068,379 m3 (2018) to 49,993,285 m3 (2019), mostly from Shahuindo and La Arena heap leach (14.7 and 16.1 Mm3); corporate new water for processing rose from 7,315,244 to 12,009,396 m3.

Precipitation reported separately from 2019 (21,241,485 m3 total, footnote: captured in tailings facilities, ponds, heap leach pads); Morococha precipitation withdrawal 12,181,279 m3 equals its 'water from precipitation' discharge exactly.

Internal inconsistency 2017: site 'discharged without use' in 303-1 (p4) does not match 306-1 (p6): e.g. Dolores 1,456,403 m3 (GW 1,247,232 + SW 209,171) vs 789,419 m3; Alamo Dorado 0 vs 155,954 m3 (equal to its groundwater used); corporate 68,916,058 vs 69,132,510 m3.

Possible copy-forward/duplicated values: 2018 La Colorada mine dewatering (4,232,942 m3, 2018 file p4) is identical to La Colorada 2017 'discharged without use' in 306-1 (2017 file p6). In 2018 Morococha third-party discharge (21,318,336) equals its mine dewatering, and Morococha surface discharge (10,113,978) matches its surface withdrawal (10,113,977); in 2019 Morococha third-party discharge (24,542,774) equals its mine dewatering and Dolores untreated surface discharge (394,537) equals its water-stress mine dewatering.

2018 groundwater withdrawal of 182,243 m3 is printed in the Alamo Dorado column, although Alamo Dorado had closed (processing ceased 2016-2017) and does not appear in the 2018 recycling or discharge tables; it may belong to another site (e.g. La Colorada, which shows '-').

Morococha volumes are strongly rainfall-driven: 2017 report notes >3x prior-year rainfall at Morococha in 2017, driving surface water discharged without use from 2,979,938 m3 (2016) to 12,761,677 m3 (2017). Huaron recycles almost no process water (0% 2017 and 2019, 5% 2018, 8.1% 2016); Dolores recycles >=91% every year.

Corporate recycling rate fell 75% (2015) -> 71% (2016) -> 65% (2017) -> 69% (2018), then 81% in 2019 with Tahoe heap-leach sites. 2016 report cover states 86% of water used in Mexican operations was recycled (PDF p2).

Water stress: only Dolores (Mexico) is reported in 'areas with water stress' (WRI Aqueduct, 2019 footnote 5); the report does not state a stress level, 'high' is set because Dolores is the only site flagged. San Vicente (Bolivia) is described as water-scarce but not WRI water-stressed (2019 file PDF p8 footnote 2).

2016 report 303-1 withdrawal table (PDF p44) does not print a unit; m3 assumed from the adjacent 306-1 table. 2019 GRI PDF has an inserted page, so PDF page numbers are one higher than printed page numbers (water tables on PDF p8-9 = printed p7-8); 2016 report PDF pages are printed page +2.
